Liver Metastasis: The patient has a history of colon cancer and has undergone right hemicolectomy. The presence of a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver, as revealed by follow-up CT, suggests the possibility of liver metastasis. The patient's normal CEA and CA19-9 levels do not rule out this diagnosis, as these markers can be normal in cases of liver metastasis.
Hepatic Cystadenocarcinoma: The patient's liver lesion has a cystic component, which could be suggestive of a hepatic cystadenocarcinoma. The absence of communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology for malignancy do not rule out this diagnosis. The patient's age and sex are also consistent with this diagnosis.
